text:
Decision-support table showing how much urea fertilizer (kg/ha) is needed, depending on a soil nitrate-N test result (ppm) and the farmer's target grain yield (1, 2, 3, or 4 t/ha). Read the soil test's NO3 ppm value on the left, then the corresponding column for the target yield:

- Soil NO3 = 0 ppm: 88 / 135 / 222 / 308 kg urea/ha (for yield targets 1/2/3/4 t/ha respectively)
- 5 ppm: 7 / 94 / 181 / 268 kg urea/ha
- 10 ppm: 0 / 53 / 140 / 227 kg urea/ha
- 15 ppm: 0 / 12 / 99 / 185 kg urea/ha
- 20 ppm: 0 / 0 / 57 / 144 kg urea/ha
- 25 ppm: 0 / 0 / 16 / 103 kg urea/ha
- 30 ppm: 0 / 0 / 0 / 62 kg urea/ha
- 35 ppm: 0 / 0 / 0 / 21 kg urea/ha
- 40 ppm and above: 0 / 0 / 0 / 0 kg urea/ha (no additional urea needed at any of these yield targets)

This table requires a laboratory soil nitrate-N test to use. As an example of how to read it: a field testing at 20 ppm soil nitrate-N, with a target yield of 3 t/ha, would need about 57 kg/ha of urea as top-up fertilizer; the same field with a 4 t/ha target would need about 144 kg/ha of urea.
